# Concept H casting set: part list (generated by `h_castings.py`; do not edit by hand)

Coarse envelope models for quoting. Near-net as-machined shape; walls, ribs, the case perimeter flange and its
bolts, oil cross-drillings, fillets and draft are not drawn. The foundry adds machining stock on every machined
face to the ISO 8062 callout for each part below (stock per side = RMA + CT/2; plan on about 7 mm on the split
face and the deck until the foundry states the grade it holds and the first-article layout shows less is enough).
Route: binder-jet printed mold + foundry pour (envelope 1.2), degassed, T6 with a certificate, radiographed before
first-op, impregnated after machining. Nothing here has been made or tested.

|---|---|---|---|
| H-101 | `ISO 8062 - CT11 - RMA 4 (G)`; the RFQ asks the foundry which grade it holds, and its answer becomes the basis | 5.0 / 6.8 / 10 | 7 on the split face (datum A) and the deck |
| H-102 | `ISO 8062 - CT11 - RMA 4 (G)`; the RFQ asks the foundry which grade it holds, and its answer becomes the basis | 5.0 / 6.8 / 10 | 7 on the split face (datum A) and the deck |
| H-201 | `ISO 8062 - CT11 - RMA 4 (G)`; the RFQ asks the foundry which grade it holds, and its answer becomes the basis | 4.8 / 6.5 / 9.5 | 7 on the deck (datum A) |

All pads are cast in the same mould half as the face they stand on, kept off the parting line and the gates [Q: the foundry places the parting line and gates, then confirms]. The secondary and tertiary pads stand on walls drafted about 2 deg, so their stated height is what stops the draft moving the part in x-y at setup (AMC/ATI casting GD&T tip, via MANUFACTURING).
